**[Gary Gygax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/E._Gary_Gygax)** Gary Gygax created [Dungeons & Dragons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungeons_%26_Dragons). He did more to inspire the imagination and bring joy than many could ever hope. If you ever enjoyed Role Playing games, this is the man you would thank. Sadly, he is now dead, but there is a Gary Gygax [Memorial Fund](http://www.gygaxmemorialfund.org/). The fund hoped to create a Gygax Tower with a bust encoiled by a dragon, in his memory, but contributions were only sufficient for a small plaque. The imagination was there, but the funding wasn't. * What would be **a good way to celebrate** the occasion? Do you have ideas in addition to organizing a game of D&D? * How could you make people less reluctant to participate? How could you **inspire people to use their imagination** tomorrow? * In what interesting, perhaps unlikely way can you see **Dungeons & Dragons in your daily life** today? Here are some **suggestions**, to fire your imagination: * **Bring dice** to work, and use them. * If people are amenable, ask them to **play the role** of a Magic User, Cleric, Bard, etc, during the course of The Day. In the workplace, **use the terms* of D&D where possible, for example, Potion, Scrolls, the Ogre on the next level... * Encourage / dare people to **reference the mythological** during meetings * Put it to people: **What would Gary Gygax do** in this situation? How would he do it? * During coffee, establish who in the office is the Lawful Evil Assassin, the Paladin, the Crypt Thing, the Shambling Mound, etc. You could try by saying, for example, "**I know who the Shrieker is**." * Reminisce: Ask others who their **favourite Character** was, why they liked them and what happened to them in the end. I would like to hear ideas of your own. And **please cross-post this information!** (An account has a daily Cross-posting limit.)

When I was very young and just got into D&D, a friends mom took 5 of us up to Lake Geneva WI for a D&D type convention. Gary was there and we were lucky enough to be picked to play in a campaign that Gary DM'd. As young kids we didn't know strategy or have the experience befitting of playing with the master and creator himself, but Gary was very cool about it and made it extremely fun for us. He was really a great guy and will always remember how down to earth and personable he was.

What a great story, /u/DrJungBrogen

At the time, did you know he was the Master? Would you please tell us a little of what you can remember from that dungeon. Was there something particularly imaginative that struck you?

Yep I'm a F.I.B. funny though, I remember those initials standing for something else lol.

We had only been playing for a little under a year, but knew who Gary was and were blown away that he showed up for the convention. I remember we got to play on a big board about 6' x 6' and Gary moved around little statues of us. There were plastic movable walls for each room or hallway in the dungeon we entered that Gary moved around as well. Gary let us choose what characters we were, but they were pre-maid, geared and assigned a level. Gary was so cool because there were times the group made bad decisions, but he always kept us alive.

Toward the end, we were getting bad dice rolls and would have easily died against a 'Beholder' because of it, but Gary planned it so without us even knowing we were leading the beholder over a certain square in the room that froze it and we attacked it freely. Was totally awesome for a bunch of 12-13 yr olds who hadn't been playing that long.

I remember Gary saying there were no rules to the game that had to be strictly followed and should be played however you think is fun. I think he liked how excited we would get when gargoyles jumped down from the ceiling or ochre jelly surrounded us. It wasn't at the level that experienced or older players would have liked, but it was incredible for us.
You certainly met a variety of monsters. It must have been funny with the gargoyles. Great story!

...up to Lake Geneva WI...
